newsitem.title: CHINA: Quality problems dog China building industry.
newsitem.headline: Quality problems dog China building industry.

text.p: China's building industry is dogged by poor design, shoddy materials, corruption and masses of untrained workers, even as central authorities strive to improve housing standards, the China Daily said on Saturday.

"The building industry is still plagued with problems like the use of substandard building materials, corruption, poor design...(and) large numbers of unqualified workers," the newspaper quoted Vice-Minister of Construction Tan Qinglian as saying.
Tan said problems in the sector had persisted despite great efforts to regulate the industry.
"It is urgent that the government strengthen law enforcement and introduce more severe punishments to firms and individuals responsible for building quality problems," Tan said.

The Construction Ministry had recently revoked the licences of eight real estate, construction and design firms for taking part in substandard building projects since 1994, Tan said, adding that 36 other companies had received warnings.
Tan said the number of building collapses had dropped to 11 in 1995 from 86 in 1985. He gave no figures for this year.
A building law aimed at setting industry standards and punishments for quality violations would be passed by the National People's Congress, or parliament, later this year, the newspaper said.
"We hope to abolish common residential building quality problems by the end of the century," Tan said.
Beijing plans to build 1.2 billion square metres (12.8 billion square ft) of housing by the year 2000.
